Alternatives to First Past the Post: Score/Range vs Instant Runoff Voting
When it comes to *single* winner voting systems as alternatives to First Past the Post (FPTP), the two that I most often see are [Instant Runoff Voting](http://www.fairvote.org/rcv) (IRV) which is ranked voting, and the [Score/Range](https://electology.org/score-voting) voting which is rated voting. There is also popular variation of Range voting know as [Approval voting](https://electology.org/approval-voting). 

When I visit fairvote.org to read up on IRV, they claim that IRV is superior to Range. When I visit electology.org they say the opposite. 

What are the pros and cons about the alternatives to FPTP? Is there an objective resource that might parse through which might be reasonable alternative in the US? It would be interesting if /r/NeutralPolitics could host a civil debate/discussion between representatives of fairvote.org and electology.org about the two systems.
